name: Small gas engines
summary: Small petrol and diesel engines, about 1–20 hp, from mowers, generators, pumps and tools.
uses: Turning a generator head or alternator
Driving a water pump, air compressor or saw
identify: Single-cylinder engines with a pull-start on mowers, generators, pressure washers, tillers, log splitters, water pumps and go-karts. Two-strokes (chainsaws, trimmers, some outboards) need oil mixed into the fuel. Never run one indoors or in a garage: the exhaust carbon monoxide kills.
test: Check the oil, then pull slowly: you should feel strong compression. Pull the plug and crank it against bare metal to look for a spark; stale fuel in the carburettor is the commonest no-start.

decay.note: Lasts. Fuel left in the carburettor gums it up within months, but cleaning fixes it.
